questions.question_text: The age of onset of this disorder is usually from adolescence or early adulthood. This disorder is associated with a suicide rate of 9%.
questions.explanation: Borderline personality disorder typically begins in adolescence or early adulthood. It is associated with impulsivity, unstable relationships, self-harm, and a high suicide rate of about 9%.

questions.question_text: Patients with this disorder usually have very low tolerance to frustration and a low threshold for discharge of aggression, including violence.
questions.explanation: Antisocial personality disorder is characterized by a history of conduct disorder before age 15, disregard for others’ safety, impulsivity, aggression, deceitfulness, and lack of remorse.

questions.question_text: Individuals with this condition usually present with the following clinical symptoms: ophthalmoplegia, nystagmus, ataxia and clouding of consciousness.
questions.explanation: Wernicke’s encephalopathy presents with the triad of ophthalmoplegia, nystagmus, and ataxia, often accompanied by confusion and clouding of consciousness.

questions.question_text: Approximately 10% of patients with this condition have the classical triad, but for others, peripheral neuropathy might also be present.
questions.explanation: Only about 10% of Wernicke’s encephalopathy cases present with the full triad; many also develop peripheral neuropathy.

questions.question_text: This is commonly described as an abnormal state in which memory and learning are affected, out of proportion to other cognitive functions in an otherwise alert and responsive patient.
questions.explanation: Korsakoff’s syndrome is characterized by severe anterograde and retrograde amnesia with relative preservation of alertness and other cognitive functions, often with confabulation.

questions.question_text: This usually occurs within 48 hours of stopping drinking.
questions.explanation: Withdrawal fits (seizures) typically occur within 48 hours after cessation of heavy alcohol use.

questions.question_text: Intoxication of alcohol usually leads to episodes of short-term amnesia and blackouts.
questions.explanation: Alcoholic blackouts are episodes of short-term amnesia during intoxication, often without loss of consciousness.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old man suffers from bipolar disorder. He has had five episodes of depression and one episode of hypomania over the past five years. He had hypothyroidism 20 years ago. He prefers to take medications. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Lamotrigine is effective for bipolar depression and prophylaxis, has no switch risk, and is preferable when hypothyroidism contraindicates lithium.

questions.question_text: A Foundation Year 2 doctor consults you regarding which anticonvulsant is not recommended for routine use in the prophylaxis in bipolar disorder. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Topiramate is not recommended for routine prophylaxis of bipolar disorder according to NICE guidelines.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old man suffers from bipolar disorder. He has had two episodes of depression and three episodes of mania over the past one year. He has not responded well to monotherapy with lithium. You suggest augmentation therapy with another medication. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Sodium valproate can be used to augment lithium in treatment-resistant bipolar disorder.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old man who suffered from bipolar disorder was treated by the psychiatrist in a tropical country. He was referred by the urologist to review his psychotropic medication as he has developed renal calculi after coming back to the UK. Which medication is associated with the development of renal calculi? (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Topiramate is associated with renal calculi, particularly in dehydrating conditions.

questions.question_text: A 45-year-old man suffers from bipolar disorder and hypertension. His GP prescribes an ACE inhibitor to treat his hypertension. The ACE inhibitor increases the serum level of one medication. (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: ACE inhibitors reduce sodium reabsorption and consequently increase lithium retention and serum levels.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old woman with rapid cycling bipolar disorder was admitted to hospital due to severe depressive symptoms. She takes lithium CR 800 mg nocte and has been adherent. Which medication would you consider to add onto the lithium? (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: In rapid cycling bipolar depression nonresponsive to lithium alone, NICE guidelines recommend adding lamotrigine.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old woman with rapid cycling bipolar disorder is managed in the community. She does not respond to monotherapy. The GP consults you on long-term management. Combination of which two medications is recommended? (Choose two options.)
questions.explanation: Long-term management of rapid cycling bipolar disorder per NICE is a combination of lithium and sodium valproate.

questions.question_text: A 20-year-old African university student preparing for pharmacology examination presents with burning headache, blurring eyesight and difficulty in understanding the meaning of the textbook, and cannot remember the drugs he studied.
questions.explanation: Brain fag is a culture-bound syndrome among African students featuring mental fatigue, headache, visual disturbance and memory problems during study.

questions.question_text: A 20-year-old Chinese national serviceman in Singapore complains that his penis is getting shorter and will go into his abdomen. He measures his penis daily and cannot concentrate on work.
questions.explanation: Koro is common in Southeast Asia and involves a delusional belief of genital retraction with fear of imminent death.

questions.question_text: A 25-year-old Malaysian woman becomes dissociative after a road traffic accident, followed by echopraxia, echolalia, command obedience and utterance of obscene words.
questions.explanation: Latah occurs in Malay women after a startling event and features exaggerated startle, echolalia, echopraxia and automatic obedience.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old indigenous Indian near Yellowknife, Canada, complains of being possessed by a spirit to eat human flesh of the tribal leader after long-term conflict with him.
questions.explanation: Windigo is a North American Indian syndrome of delusional belief in cannibalistic transformation by a spirit.

questions.question_text: She has a mask-like face and shows no feelings at all.
questions.explanation: Flat affect is a lack of emotional expression and a mask-like facial appearance.

questions.question_text: She stands perplexed at the door, putting one hand forward and then taking it back.
questions.explanation: Ambivalence is the simultaneous presence of opposing feelings toward a single object or action.

questions.question_text: She shouts and damages the door after she knows that she cannot go for home leave this weekend.
questions.explanation: Acting-out is the direct expression of unconscious wishes or impulses with overt actions.

questions.question_text: In this experiment, an 11-month infant was allowed to play with a white rat. At this point, the infant showed no fear of the rat. The investigator made a loud sound whenever the infant touched the rat. Two weeks later, the infant showed fear of the rat and rabbit even though there was no loud sound.
questions.explanation: John Watson conducted the Little Albert experiment to demonstrate conditioned fear and stimulus generalization.

questions.question_text: In this experiment, a hungry cat was confined in a puzzle box with food visible on the outside. The cat could manipulate some devices to open the gate of the puzzle box. Foods were placed outside the box, and the food served as an incentive for the cat to open the gate. Initially, the cat first behaved aimlessly as if doing things by trial and error. The presence of food made the opening of gate more likely to occur and the cat took less time to get the food after repeated trials.
questions.explanation: Edward Thorndike formulated the law of effect based on puzzle‐box experiments with cats, demonstrating trial-and-error learning.

questions.question_text: In this experiment, a dog was placed in a two-compartment box where there was no escape. After repeated failures to escape, the dog realized that there was an absence of contingency, became withdrawn and stopped jumping from one compartment to another.
questions.explanation: Martin Seligman demonstrated learned helplessness when dogs ceased trying to escape in inescapable shock experiments.

questions.question_text: The investigator designed a box that had one or more levers. When a starved rat pressed the lever, a small pellet of food was dropped onto a tray. The rat soon learned that when he pressed the lever he would receive some food.
questions.explanation: B.F. Skinner used the operant chamber (Skinner box) to demonstrate positive and negative reinforcement in rats.

questions.question_text: In this experiment, a child witnessed the different levels of aggression from an adult towards a doll. The child paid attention to the relevant aspects of aggression and created a visual image of the model in her mind. By repeated observations, the child remembered the aggressive behaviour. The child rehearsed the aggressive behaviour and anticipated similar consequences between herself and the adult.
questions.explanation: Albert Bandura conducted the Bobo doll experiment demonstrating observational (social) learning and vicarious reinforcement.

questions.question_text: The investigator performed a minor operation on a dog to relocate its salivary duct to the outside of its cheek. This allowed easy measurement of saliva. Periodically, a bell was rang, followed shortly thereafter by meat being placed in the dog’s mouth.
questions.explanation: Ivan Pavlov’s classical conditioning experiments measured salivary response in dogs to a bell paired with food.

questions.question_text: This investigator constructed problems involving obtaining food not directly accessible for chimpanzees. Initially they spent time unproductively, then all of a sudden piled boxes to reach bananas.
questions.explanation: Wolfgang Köhler studied insight learning in chimpanzees, who suddenly solved problems by rearranging elements.

questions.question_text: This investigator designed complex maze running experiments and investigated reinforcement in learning. Rats developed cognitive maps even without reward, leading to latent learning theory.
questions.explanation: Edward Tolman’s maze studies demonstrated latent learning: rats formed cognitive maps even in the absence of reward.

questions.question_text: This investigator conducted experiments using monkeys and found that more probable behaviours would reinforce less probable behaviours.
questions.explanation: David Premack’s principle states that a higher-probability behaviour can reinforce a lower-probability behaviour.
